title: Useful parallelism: continuity groups, boundary contracts, a sting is one builder, workers grow only with evidence
note: Synthetic. Lists the function exercised, the input and the expected outcome; authored, not run. No number here is a measurement of real rendering, latency, memory or cost.

calls.case: 5 scenes: s1-s2 joined by a morph seam, s3 independent behind a hard cut, s4-s5 share a character component across a hard cut
a link of type deliberate_discontinuity between s2 and s3
a boundary between groups with a link of type same_object and no boundary contract
policy build_workers.start 3, 6 ready independent scene groups, usage known, no observations
the same with observations: tput(3)=2.0/min, tput(2)=1.5/min, queue wait 20 s
the same but queue wait 300 s
a 12 s film with 2 scenes; and a direct film
usage unreported (usage_known false) and provider throttled

expect: groups are [s1,s2], [s3], [s4,s5] with reasons naming the morph seam and the persistent character; the hard cut between s2 and s3 is a low-coupling boundary needing only start_end_time
a deliberate discontinuity never joins scenes

the cross-group boundary reports status needs_contract and missing lists the fields the lead (shared components owner) must write: semantic_objects, positions_units, camera_crop, scale, color_treatment, velocity_transform
without observations workers = min(start, ready) = 3, never 6 or 8-12
with a >=15% throughput gain and a short queue wait the count grows by one; with no gain it stays put
a long heavy-resource queue wait shrinks the count by one
a sting or a direct film is one builder with the reason stated
unknown usage caps at 2 and a throttled provider drops one more; every decision lists reasons and basis proposed
